name: Introduction and overview — Iowa-class Battleship — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Iowa-class Battleship
description: Introduction and overview of the Iowa-class Battleship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Iowa class — four ships — were the ultimate battleships: 58,000 tons, 33 knots, and nine 16-inch/50 guns that could throw a shell 23 miles. Iowas served in WWII, Korea, and were reactivated in the 1980s with Tomahawk missiles for the Cold War. All four are museum ships; Missouri hosted Japan's surrender. Baseline facts: U.S. battleship; 4 built; nine 16-inch guns; WWII/Korea/1980s; all museums..

The Iowa class — four ships — were the ultimate battleships: 58,000 tons, 33 knots, and nine 16-inch/50 guns that could throw a shell 23 miles. Iowas served in WWII, Korea, and were reactivated in the 1980s with Tomahawk missiles for the Cold War. All four are museum ships; Missouri hosted Japan's surrender. Baseline facts: U.S. battleship; 4 built; nine 16-inch guns; WWII/Korea/1980s; all museums..
